content.text: Before you start this guide, you should have followed all the other ironworker guides to build the different modules.
This guide will walk you through putting them all together into a complete machine.

introduction_raw:
Before you start this guide, you should have followed all the other ironworker guides to build the different modules.

This guide will walk you through putting them all together into a complete machine.
introduction_rendered:
Before you start this guide, you should have followed all the other ironworker guides to build the different modules.

This guide will walk you through putting them all together into a complete machine.

lines.text_raw: TODO I don't think this video should be in the guide. It more about the process of documenting it and talks about disassembling which may be confusing to people. It doesn't add any info.
lines.text_rendered: TODO I don't think this video should be in the guide. It more about the process of documenting it and talks about disassembling which may be confusing to people. It doesn't add any info.

lines.text_raw: Use the hoist to lift the upper frame into place, making sure the pivot plate holes roughly align.
lines.text_rendered: Use the hoist to lift the upper frame into place, making sure the pivot plate holes roughly align.

lines.text_raw: Dill out the threads of each nut using a 1" drill bit.
lines.text_rendered: Dill out the threads of each nut using a 1" drill bit.

lines.text_raw: Put a bolt through a drilled out nut, the bottom hole of the plates on the frame, 2 washers, the piston side of the cylinder, 2 more washers, the other plates, and another drilled out nut. Make sure the hose connectors on the hydraulic cylinder face away from the rest of the ironworker.
lines.text_rendered: Put a bolt through a drilled out nut, the bottom hole of the plates on the frame, 2 washers, the piston side of the cylinder, 2 more washers, the other plates, and another drilled out nut. Make sure the hose connectors on the hydraulic cylinder face away from the rest of the ironworker.

lines.text_raw: Put a nut on the bolt but don't tighten all the way.
lines.text_rendered: Put a nut on the bolt but don't tighten all the way.

lines.text_raw: If you have trouble getting the bolt through, try using an impact wrench to drive it through. If that doesn't work, it may help to loosen the plates with the welded nuts. Make sure not to put in too many spacers while they're loose and to tighten them when you're done.
lines.text_rendered: If you have trouble getting the bolt through, try using an impact wrench to drive it through. If that doesn't work, it may help to loosen the plates with the welded nuts. Make sure not to put in too many spacers while they're loose and to tighten them when you're done.

lines.text_raw: Put a bolt through a drilled out nut, the bottom hole of the plates on the frame, 2 washers, the base side of the cylinder, 1 more washer (on ours there was only room for 3 spacer washers), the other plates, and the last drilled out nut. Make sure the hose connectors on the hydraulic cylinder face away from the rest of the ironworker.
lines.text_rendered: Put a bolt through a drilled out nut, the bottom hole of the plates on the frame, 2 washers, the base side of the cylinder, 1 more washer (on ours there was only room for 3 spacer washers), the other plates, and the last drilled out nut. Make sure the hose connectors on the hydraulic cylinder face away from the rest of the ironworker.

lines.text_raw: Put a nut on the bolt and tighten it and the top one.
lines.text_rendered: Put a nut on the bolt and tighten it and the top one.

lines.text_raw: Weld each of the 4 drilled out nuts to the pivot plates.
lines.text_rendered: Weld each of the 4 drilled out nuts to the pivot plates.

lines.text_raw: Adjust the hoist so that the pivot plate holes line up perfectly.
lines.text_rendered: Adjust the hoist so that the pivot plate holes line up perfectly.

lines.text_raw: Tighten the 8 nuts that hold on the pivot plates. They should be tight enough to hold the pivot plates flat, but not so tight that the plates can't wiggle slightly.
lines.text_rendered: Tighten the 8 nuts that hold on the pivot plates. They should be tight enough to hold the pivot plates flat, but not so tight that the plates can't wiggle slightly.

lines.text_raw: 1 3" x 8" solid shaft (cut a length if you've got a longer piece)
lines.text_rendered: 1 3" x 8" solid shaft (cut a length if you've got a longer piece)

lines.text_raw: Weld a 1" nut to each end of the shaft.
lines.text_rendered: Weld a 1" nut to each end of the shaft.

lines.text_raw: In the picture we put a bolt into the nut temporarily to hold it in place while welding.
lines.text_rendered: In the picture we put a bolt into the nut temporarily to hold it in place while welding.

lines.text_raw: Put grease on the shaft and push it through the pivot plate holes using an impact wrench on the nut welded to the shaft. Each end of the shaft should line up with the outermost pivot plate with a bushing which is the 3rd plate in from each side.
lines.text_rendered: Put grease on the shaft and push it through the pivot plate holes using an impact wrench on the nut welded to the shaft. Each end of the shaft should line up with the outermost pivot plate with a bushing which is the 3rd plate in from each side.

lines.text_raw: If you're having trouble getting it all the way through, here are some things to try:
lines.text_rendered: If you're having trouble getting it all the way through, here are some things to try:

lines.text_raw: Add or remove weight on the shaft by raising or lowering the hoist.
lines.text_rendered: Add or remove weight on the shaft by raising or lowering the hoist.

lines.text_raw: Tighten or loosen the bolts holding the pivot plates.
lines.text_rendered: Tighten or loosen the bolts holding the pivot plates.

lines.text_raw: Make sure all the pivot plates are lined up properly.
lines.text_rendered: Make sure all the pivot plates are lined up properly.

lines.text_raw: If you still can't get it quite all the way through leave it for now. As long as it's close, you'll be able to pull it the rest of the way through with the pinch plates in a couple of steps.
lines.text_rendered: If you still can't get it quite all the way through leave it for now. As long as it's close, you'll be able to pull it the rest of the way through with the pinch plates in a couple of steps.

lines.text_raw: Put the cubes in between the pivot plates on either side of the shaft. Rest them on little pieces of wood temporarily so that they're bout 1/2" above the tube below them.
lines.text_rendered: Put the cubes in between the pivot plates on either side of the shaft. Rest them on little pieces of wood temporarily so that they're bout 1/2" above the tube below them.

lines.text_raw: They should be tightened with about 150 ft-lbs of force since they're critical for keeping the blades perfectly aligned during cutting.
lines.text_rendered: They should be tightened with about 150 ft-lbs of force since they're critical for keeping the blades perfectly aligned during cutting.

lines.text_raw: 1 1" x 8" x 16" plate (it can be longer than 16")
lines.text_rendered: 1 1" x 8" x 16" plate (it can be longer than 16")

lines.text_raw: The picture shows 7"x7" plates because we had 7" stock handy. They do the job, but we recommend 8".
lines.text_rendered: The picture shows 7"x7" plates because we had 7" stock handy. They do the job, but we recommend 8".

lines.text_raw: Make holes in the center of each 8"x8" plate big enough for 1" bolts. We drilled starter holes and then used an acetylene torch to widen them.
lines.text_rendered: Make holes in the center of each 8"x8" plate big enough for 1" bolts. We drilled starter holes and then used an acetylene torch to widen them.

lines.text_raw: Take a 2"x1" bolt, put a washer on it, put it through the 8"x8" plate, and screw it loosely into the bolt at the end of the shaft. Then repeat on the other side.
lines.text_rendered: Take a 2"x1" bolt, put a washer on it, put it through the 8"x8" plate, and screw it loosely into the bolt at the end of the shaft. Then repeat on the other side.

lines.text_raw: If the shaft isn't centered, first put on the plate on the side where the shaft isn't far enough through. Tighten the plate until you see on the other side that the shaft is centered.
lines.text_rendered: If the shaft isn't centered, first put on the plate on the side where the shaft isn't far enough through. Tighten the plate until you see on the other side that the shaft is centered.

lines.text_raw: The point of these bolts and plates is to pinch the pivot joint as tightly together as possible. They should be tightened with about 150 ft-lbs of force.
lines.text_rendered: The point of these bolts and plates is to pinch the pivot joint as tightly together as possible. They should be tightened with about 150 ft-lbs of force.

lines.text_raw: You want the bolt to be most of the way through the shaft nut when fully tightened. If it looks like the bolt will be too long for the nut and will bottom out against the shaft, add more washers. If it looks like the bolt won't get almost all the way through the nut, take out the washer.
lines.text_rendered: You want the bolt to be most of the way through the shaft nut when fully tightened. If it looks like the bolt will be too long for the nut and will bottom out against the shaft, add more washers. If it looks like the bolt won't get almost all the way through the nut, take out the washer.

lines.text_raw: Remove the wooden supports holding up the 2 cubes in the pivot if they're still there. The pressure from the pivot plates should hold them in place.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the wooden supports holding up the 2 cubes in the pivot if they're still there. The pressure from the pivot plates should hold them in place.

lines.text_raw: Lay the 6 plates on the lower frame in the middle.
lines.text_rendered: Lay the 6 plates on the lower frame in the middle.

lines.text_raw: The picture show 3 of the plates shorter. That's a mistake! They should all be 5 holes (20" long).
lines.text_rendered: The picture show 3 of the plates shorter. That's a mistake! They should all be 5 holes (20" long).

lines.text_raw: Put the lower blade assembly in place so it's hanging off the 6 plates with the blade face up.
lines.text_rendered: Put the lower blade assembly in place so it's hanging off the 6 plates with the blade face up.

lines.text_raw: Adjust the blade assembly and the riser plates so the row of hole closest to the edge of the 2 x 4 hole plate lines up with the holes in the lower frame tube, and the riser plates extend about 1" past the left edge of the blade towards the pivot.
lines.text_rendered: Adjust the blade assembly and the riser plates so the row of hole closest to the edge of the 2 x 4 hole plate lines up with the holes in the lower frame tube, and the riser plates extend about 1" past the left edge of the blade towards the pivot.

lines.text_raw: Put the bolts through washers, the lower blade mount plate, the lower frame, another set of washers, and put on the nuts. Hand tighten them.
lines.text_rendered: Put the bolts through washers, the lower blade mount plate, the lower frame, another set of washers, and put on the nuts. Hand tighten them.

lines.text_raw: 1 16.5" x 1" threaded rod (TODO link to guide on cutting threaded rod)
lines.text_rendered: 1 16.5" x 1" threaded rod (TODO link to guide on cutting threaded rod)

lines.text_raw: Put a piece of plywood or some other spacer on the lower blade and rest the four plates on it.
lines.text_rendered: Put a piece of plywood or some other spacer on the lower blade and rest the four plates on it.

lines.text_raw: Put a nut and washer on on end of the threaded rod and put it through from the top of the upper frame down through the plates.
lines.text_rendered: Put a nut and washer on on end of the threaded rod and put it through from the top of the upper frame down through the plates.

lines.text_raw: Put a nut below the plates without a washer. Hand tighten.
lines.text_rendered: Put a nut below the plates without a washer. Hand tighten.

lines.text_raw: Put the four bolts with washers through the upper frame. The bolts should go through the washers, then through the frame from the side where the hydraulic cylinder is on the right.
lines.text_rendered: Put the four bolts with washers through the upper frame. The bolts should go through the washers, then through the frame from the side where the hydraulic cylinder is on the right.

lines.text_raw: Put the upper blade support over the bolts from the side where the cylinder is on the left.
lines.text_rendered: Put the upper blade support over the bolts from the side where the cylinder is on the left.

lines.text_raw: Put washers and nuts on the top blade support bolts and hand tighten.
lines.text_rendered: Put washers and nuts on the top blade support bolts and hand tighten.

lines.text_raw: TODO press and tighten blades in new steps
lines.text_rendered: TODO press and tighten blades in new steps

lines.text_raw: Put the table assembly threaded rods through the frame from the side with the lower blade. They should go through the holes on either side of the lower blade plate.
lines.text_rendered: Put the table assembly threaded rods through the frame from the side with the lower blade. They should go through the holes on either side of the lower blade plate.

lines.text_raw: TODO from mon- reorg this to have threaded rods in this guide. 17" rods. 5 washers. clamp structure and work surface struture separately. clamp bolts 13"
lines.text_rendered: TODO from mon- reorg this to have threaded rods in this guide. 17" rods. 5 washers. clamp structure and work surface struture separately. clamp bolts 13"

lines.text_raw: TODO fix bot mid plate everywhere i took pics on mon
lines.text_rendered: TODO fix bot mid plate everywhere i took pics on mon

lines.text_raw: Put a washer and nut on the end of each rod holding the table.
lines.text_rendered: Put a washer and nut on the end of each rod holding the table.

lines.text_raw: 2 ounces of grease (I made up 2 oz, Marcin should verify)
lines.text_rendered: 2 ounces of grease (I made up 2 oz, Marcin should verify)

lines.text_raw: Apply grease to both sides of the top part of the frame as shown in the picture. Squeeze some out using the gun and then smear it around.
lines.text_rendered: Apply grease to both sides of the top part of the frame as shown in the picture. Squeeze some out using the gun and then smear it around.

lines.text_raw: put the washer onto threaded rod and screw the nut onto one end
lines.text_rendered: put the washer onto threaded rod and screw the nut onto one end

lines.text_raw: Put three threaded rods through the uprights and tubes on the bottom hole, fourth hole up, and top hole of the uprights.
lines.text_rendered: Put three threaded rods through the uprights and tubes on the bottom hole, fourth hole up, and top hole of the uprights.

lines.text_raw: Put the two upright on either side of the frame near the cylinder as shown.
lines.text_rendered: Put the two upright on either side of the frame near the cylinder as shown.

lines.text_raw: Put threaded rods through the bottom hole, 4th from the bottom hole, and top hole of the uprights. Do NOT put any through the top part of the frame since it needs to be able to move up and down.
lines.text_rendered: Put threaded rods through the bottom hole, 4th from the bottom hole, and top hole of the uprights. Do NOT put any through the top part of the frame since it needs to be able to move up and down.

lines.text_raw: The uprights make sure the bottom and top stay in perfect alignment so the nuts have to be very tight. Use a hydraulic system to open the ironworker all the way and then use 150 ft-lbs of force when tightening these 3 bolts.
lines.text_rendered: The uprights make sure the bottom and top stay in perfect alignment so the nuts have to be very tight. Use a hydraulic system to open the ironworker all the way and then use 150 ft-lbs of force when tightening these 3 bolts.

lines.text_raw: Adjusted the table so that both surface of the table is at the same height as the edge of the blade.
lines.text_rendered: Adjusted the table so that both surface of the table is at the same height as the edge of the blade.

lines.text_raw: To do this, raise the table with the floor jack after loosening table-holding bolts and raise the table level to match the blade edge level.
lines.text_rendered: To do this, raise the table with the floor jack after loosening table-holding bolts and raise the table level to match the blade edge level.

lines.text_raw: Once the table level is set than retighten the table-holding bolts.
lines.text_rendered: Once the table level is set than retighten the table-holding bolts.

lines.text_raw: Use 9 hole tubes, quarter inch wall.
lines.text_rendered: Use 9 hole tubes, quarter inch wall.

lines.text_raw: Bolt rear legs to the stabilizer tubes using a 23" length of threaded rod
lines.text_rendered: Bolt rear legs to the stabilizer tubes using a 23" length of threaded rod

lines.text_raw: Cut the leg and feet tubes to size
lines.text_rendered: Cut the leg and feet tubes to size

lines.text_raw: Use the hoist to lay the machine on its side
lines.text_rendered: Use the hoist to lay the machine on its side

lines.text_raw: Take off the temporary legs to facilitate moving the machine outside
lines.text_rendered: Take off the temporary legs to facilitate moving the machine outside

lines.text_raw: Hoist the machine up to stand on the rear legs
lines.text_rendered: Hoist the machine up to stand on the rear legs

lines.text_raw: Raise the front of the machine after it stands on the rear legs
lines.text_rendered: Raise the front of the machine after it stands on the rear legs
